anomalies.observed: The MCU's PB14 (U2 pin 35) is no longer on the DISP_SDA net. It sits only on Net-(U5-Pad2), which connects to the input (pin 2) of a 74LVC1G34 buffer U5. The buffer's output (pin 4) drives DISP_SDA, which feeds R7's pull-up and the SSD1306 D1/D2 pins. The DISP_SDA net therefore has no direct connection to the MCU.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes DISP_SDA as a direct, bidirectional link: U2 pin 35 (PB14) to R7 (10 kΩ pull-up) to U4 pins 19/20 (D1/D2). It lists no buffer, and the component table has no U5.

evidence.quote: `DISP_SDA`: U2 pin 35 (`PB14`) — R7 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U4 pins 19/20 (`D1`/`D2`)

anomalies.impact: The I2C bus to the OLED becomes one-way. The MCU cannot see the display's ACK or read-back on SDA, and a buffer whose enable or direction is not controlled adds a propagation delay and an unintended driver on the bus. Display communication is likely to fail or behave unreliably.

anomalies.observed: STM32L476 VBAT pin 1 is on its own net, unconnected-(U2-VBAT-Pad1), with no connection to VCC or any other supply.
anomalies.expected: The STM32 datasheet requires VBAT to be powered at all times, either from a battery or tied to VDD. The specification does not mention leaving it open.
anomalies.impact: The RTC and backup domain may be unpowered, and the device may behave unreliably. This may be an inherited property of the reference design rather than a tampering artefact.

parsed.summary: The netlist inserts a 74LVC1G34 buffer (U5) into the display SDA path, which is not in the specification and turns the bidirectional I2C line into a one-way drive from the MCU. This is the most likely deviation. A lower-confidence secondary concern is that the MCU's VBAT pin is left unconnected.
